headline: Readiness stayed red and today's Un1t class still ran hot (70% in Z3-Z4) — the grey-zone pattern the week-review flagged is repeating. Protect tonight's sleep before tomorrow's long run.
body_state: Fitness 2.0's composite reads 38.1/low, driven by sleep: HRV 37ms overnight (below your personal band), sleep score 72 off just 6.1h, and 14-day sleep debt now ~25h. Body Battery started at 38, only +37 overnight recharge. TSB sits at -14.15 — genuinely inside the -5…-30 productive band, and Garmin tags training status "Productive" — but the recovery layer overrides that: HRV and sleep debt say protect today regardless of what the load number says.
session: No running-plan session today — the 13km long run is tomorrow (08-16). The calendar's "Un1t training" (45min Cardio) already ran this morning and is logged: 70% of it sat in Z3-Z4 (avg HR 135, max 178), the same moderate-hard intensity Un1t sessions have carried all month — landing on exactly the day the readiness call said "easy running only." That's done and can't be undone. What matters now is adding nothing else today and giving tonight's sleep the best shot at recovering before tomorrow's long run — check HRV/Battery in the morning before committing to it at full length.
recent: Grey-zone pattern continuing: Thursday's easy run (planned 7km) was cut to 5.46km and finished at 4:28/km, HR 159-166 — a fast, non-easy finish on a readiness-36 day. Wednesday's tempo also undershot (5.43km vs 7km) and never reached threshold HR (143 vs LT 163) despite RPE 8 — a fatigue signal, not a fitness one. Tuesday's and today's Un1t classes both ran 50-70% of their time in zone 3-4. Four candidate "easy" sessions this week, none of them actually easy — the week-review's grey-zone limiter is the through-line.
focus: Nothing more today — sleep debt (~25h) is the real limiter, not training load
Gate tomorrow's 13km long run on morning HRV/Battery, not just the calendar
Un1t keeps landing Z3-Z4 on red days — self-pace it down or skip when the morning call says easy
